text.tspan: We wondered what a gene regulation mechanism that accounts for this biological reality
would look like. I started by building intuition with lattice simulations of polymers
in 3D space interacting with dilute molecules, representing regulatory proteins.
Here the orange segment of DNA represents a promoter near the gene, and the red
segment is a distant enhancer. blue particle attach to both orange and red, and to each
other. The black dot here is the place where RNA polymerase binds and launches
transcription. Blue particles represent regulatory molecules, both TF and RNA Pol.
Transcription initiates whenever a blue particle attaches to the black dot.
You can see that because blue particles condense on the regulatory regions,
and because they are attracted to each other, they act like glue. This glue acts at very short
range, it cannot bring distant parts of DNA together. However, when they do happen to come
in contact, it keeps them close together much longer than they would otherwise.
